summary: Privacy-focused Tauri browser shell with passing TypeScript, policy, Rust, production build, session isolation, permission, download, audit, WebView contract, and live WebView binding validation. Recent work fixed silent-failure bugs, an isolation-scope cleanup leak, a disconnected vault bookmark count, corrected UI/audit claims that overstated session isolation as real storage separation, replaced the encrypted-export key derivation with Argon2id, moved the permission/download decision registries from in-memory-only to SQLite persistence, added SQLCipher at-rest encryption with the key stored in the OS keychain, and -- at explicit user direction, scope agreed in advance -- migrated the live WebView from an iframe to a real native child webview with genuine Rust-enforced download and navigation policy.
current_objective: Validate the live WebView privacy boundary through bounded manual use. Architecture expansion happens only at explicit user direction with scope agreed in advance, not proactively; keep claims honest as gaps are found.
next_action: No specific outstanding action. Two things remain open by design: permission-callback integration (blocked on tauri not yet wrapping wry 0.56's permission API) and inline-content-type download detection (no fix possible with Tauri's current public API for external URLs). Both re-check when Tauri ships the relevant API.
known_gaps: Session isolation is TypeScript-layer bookkeeping only; there is one shared WebView, so cookies/storage are not actually partitioned per profile.
Permission-callback integration (camera/mic/geolocation) is blocked on tauri not yet wrapping wry 0.56.0's permission-request API.

Content a site renders inline instead of forcing a download (e.g. a PDF export) is not caught by download blocking; Tauri's on_web_resource_request is documented as tauri-protocol-only, not applicable to external URLs.
constraints: Do not add a new browser subsystem or expand architecture proactively -- only at explicit user direction with scope agreed in advance.
Do not weaken download blocking or permission prompting.
Do not treat smoke tests as proof of packaged desktop behavior.
Manual validation must use bounded, non-sensitive test URLs and content.
Do not let UI copy, audit events, or the threat model claim privacy guarantees that aren't actually implemented.
